verify_hint: Check the query_database handler in build_server for every place _QUERY_META_KEY is set, including the AgentRunError handler
evidence: server.py:520-523 is the only place _QUERY_META_KEY is set (grep of server.py), wrapping query_info in outgoing_query_info(..., as_written=has_rewriting_guard(cfg)). outgoing_query_info (tools/query_database.py:529-540) returns a new dict and never mutates the input. query_database_impl_with_widgets returns the raw query_info (line 941); _append_sql_block (543-564) only builds the markdown text from a local sql variable, no mutation. On AgentRunError (server.py:500-512) the handler uses _agent_error_result (175-203), whose meta holds only the conversation key and optionally the agent trace; no sqllens/query key. AgentRunError carries query_info as an attribute (query_database.py:931,938) but the server never copies it into _meta. Absolute-claim input traced: a rewriting-guard config with is_error true -> AgentRunError with query_info -> handler emits no query key and no note.

the SQL starts with the line ``-- SQL Lens applies this server's access

(line-wrapped, single spaces). AS_WRITTEN_NOTE_LINE at query_database.py:510-513 is '-- SQL Lens applies this server's access rules to queries before running them, so the query that ran can differ from this text.' claim: config.py show_details description says SQL is labelled the query as written with a rule-set file or [[rls]] rules because access rules change it before it runs.
source_excerpt:
"Append the SQL the agent wrote to query answers (with a rule-set file "
            "or [[rls]] rules, labelled as the query as written, since access rules "
            "change it before it runs). OFF by default: exposing "
verify_hint: Check has_rewriting_guard condition matches the 'rule-set file or [[rls]] rules' scope
evidence: has_rewriting_guard (src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:516-522) returns cfg.rule_sets.loaded is not None or bool(cfg.rls), exactly the 'rule-set file or [[rls]] rules' scope. build_agent (src/sqllens/agent/factory.py:127-134) wires RlsGuardRunner when cfg.rls is non-empty and RuleSetGuardRunner when a rule set is loaded; both rewrite SQL before it runs. The call sites query_database.py:940 and server.py:522 pass as_written=has_rewriting_guard(cfg), so the label applies under those conditions. The config.py:529-532 description matches.

claim: _GuardedAgent emits run_sql cards and a STATUS_CARD with metadata {'sql': ...} shaped like the real agent's run_sql tool output, so components_to_blocks builds query_info and agent_trace as it would in production.
verify_against: src/sqllens/agent/tools run_sql tool status card emission and src/sqllens/tools/_format.py components_to_blocks
verify_hint: Compare make_tool_cards/make_status_card in tests/unit/_agent_stubs.py with the real run_sql tool's UiComponent output
evidence: The claimed lines 352-381 do not exist (the file has 297 lines); _GuardedAgent is at tests/unit/test_query_as_written.py:77-107. Its _stream yields make_tool_cards('run_sql', {'sql': ...}) and then a success STATUS_CARD with metadata={'sql': ...}. The real agent (src/sqllens/agent/core/agent/agent.py:781-787, 955-962) emits a 'running' StatusCard 'Executing {tool}' with metadata=tool_call.arguments, then a completion card from set_status with the same metadata. The run_sql tool itself (agent/tools/run_sql.py) emits no status card, only a DataFrame/notification component. tests/unit/_agent_stubs.py:98-148 mirrors the running/completed pair with the same id and metadata=args. components_to_blocks (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:374-435) reads metadata['sql'] from STATUS_CARDs, so it builds query_info from them. The extra explicit success card duplicates the completion card; this is harmless because the 'last wins' logic treats identical SQL the same.

claim: _Recorder.run_sql matches the SqlRunner.run_sql signature (args, context, require_base_tables keyword) that RuleSetGuardRunner and RlsGuardRunner call.
verify_against: src/sqllens/agent/capabilities/sql_runner SqlRunner and the guard runners' calls
verify_hint: Check SqlRunner.run_sql and how RuleSetGuardRunner / RlsGuardRunner invoke the inner runner
evidence: The claim's source_line 344 is out of range (file has 297 lines); _Recorder is at tests/unit/test_query_as_written.py:66-74. Its run_sql(self, args: RunSqlToolArgs, context: ToolContext, *, require_base_tables: bool = False) is identical to the abstract SqlRunner.run_sql (src/sqllens/agent/capabilities/sql_runner/base.py:22-24). RuleSetGuardRunner calls inner.run_sql(args_copy, context, require_base_tables=True) (src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:894-896). RlsGuardRunner calls inner.run_sql(args_copy, context, **options) with options either {} or {require_base_tables: True} (src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py:231-233). Every call form is accepted by the recorder.

claim: Patching rule_sets._check_catalog_blocking is enough to bypass the catalog check the turn performs for a loaded rule-set file.
verify_hint: Check rule_sets.py around line 1233 and whether query_database imports the function by name
evidence: The test file has 297 lines (line 337 absent); the patch is the confirmed_catalog fixture at tests/unit/test_query_as_written.py:62-63, monkeypatching sqllens.rule_sets._check_catalog_blocking. query_database.py:37,782 imports and calls ensure_catalog_confirmed, not _check_catalog_blocking. ensure_catalog_confirmed (rule_sets.py:1233) resolves _check_catalog_blocking via a module-global lookup at call time, so the patched attribute is used; the only caller of _check_catalog_blocking in src is that line. The bypass therefore holds. Once the lambda returns None, state.confirmed is set (line 1244) and the real pymysql check never runs.

claim: The test asserts the note line changes nothing MySQL runs, by comparing sqlglot output with comments stripped.
source_excerpt: def test_note_line_changes_nothing_mysql_runs() -> None:
verify_hint: Trace a model SQL whose first token is a MySQL executable comment or a line ending in a backslash: does prefixing a -- line change the parse?
evidence: The test (tests/unit/test_query_as_written.py:188-192; source_line 462 is stale) parses f"{NOTE}\n{RULE_SET_SQL}" and RULE_SET_SQL with sqlglot read='mysql' and compares .sql(dialect='mysql', comments=False) for both, which is exactly the claimed comparison. NOTE (line 45-48, identical to AS_WRITTEN_NOTE_LINE in src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:510-513) starts with '-- ' (dash dash space), a MySQL line comment, has no backslash and no newline, so it ends at the newline separator. Hostile input traced: a model SQL beginning with a /*! */ executable comment or ending lines in a backslash is unaffected, because the prefix comment is closed by the newline before the SQL begins. Limitation: the test only exercises one plain SELECT and sqlglot, not a MySQL server, but the claim describes what the test does and it does so.
